items.title: Watch: Coyote chases bear away from Los Angeles home
items.comment: A bear wandered up to a Los Angeles home and was promptly run off by a coyote roughly a fifth its size. The footage settles nothing about the food chain.

items.title: Watch: Dog who spent 72 days lost in mountains wins Hambone Award
items.comment: A golden retriever bolted on Christmas Day near Lake Tahoe and spent 72 days in the mountains before a shelter scanned his microchip. Thin but unhurt, he came home and then won a national award for it.

items.title: Watch: Texas police apprehend lemur on the loose
items.comment: Belton officers were dispatched to a lemur at large and described the suspect as fast, furry, and refusing to cooperate. He was detained and returned to his owner, because Texas lets you keep one of these.

items.title: Wanted Florida man caught hiding under mattress yells for mom who tried to punch officer: WHPD
items.comment: Officers spotted a suspiciously large lump in the middle of a mattress and lifted it to find their wanted man underneath. He immediately started yelling for his mother, who came running and made the situation considerably worse.

items.title: Watch: Florida man breaks own record with mini basketball shot from 102 feet
items.comment: A Tampa man sank a miniature basketball from 102 feet — longer than a full court — to break the world record he already held. He trained for this at Pop-a-Shot.

items.title: Junction City parking update ends move-a-few-inches loophole
items.comment: For years, drivers beat the time limit by rolling forward a few inches to reset the clock. The city has now written an ordinance specifically to end the shuffle.

items.title: St. Clair Shores man fined $15K for docking boats, attorney calls ordinance unconstitutional
items.comment: A Michigan man was fined $15,000 for docking boats at his own property. His attorney's characterization of the penalty is not printable in a family publication.

items.title: Resort island POA fined SC man after he railed against them online. Now he's suing.
items.comment: A resort island property owners association fined a man for the things he wrote about them online. He is now suing, which is unlikely to improve his standing with the board.

items.title: Florida man pulled over on lawn mower busted for meth and weed
items.comment: A deputy pulled over a red riding lawn mower on a public road because it was not, in any legal sense, a vehicle. The bag between the driver's feet turned out to hold meth, pills, and weed.

items.title: HOA lawsuit leaves Horn Rapids homeowners in limbo
items.comment: A lawsuit has left homeowners in the Horn Rapids community stuck in limbo while their HOA fights it out. Nobody who bought a house there signed up to be a party to litigation.

items.title: Ligonier Man Arrested For Allegedly Breaking Into Taco Bell Restaurant
items.comment: An Indiana man is accused of breaking into a Taco Bell after hours. Whatever he was after, the restaurant is open most of the day and takes cash.

items.title: Man polishing powder horn outside Lexington church prompts bizarre police response
items.comment: A man stood outside a Lexington church quietly polishing a powder horn, and the police response escalated accordingly. In the town where the Revolution started, this is arguably just a hobby.

items.title: Man arrested for allegedly sneaking onto JetBlue plane in Florida
items.comment: A Florida man climbed a barbed-wire fence, went up the maintenance stairs, let himself in an unlocked door of a parked JetBlue jet, and fell asleep in the restroom. The crew found him there the next morning when they went to move the plane.
items.source_name: ABC News - Breaking News, Latest News and Videos

items.title: Florida man wins $358,104 lottery prize during Michigan trip
items.comment: A 75-year-old Florida man visiting family in Michigan kept up his Fantasy 5 habit at a gas station there and hit for $358,104. He is using it to buy a house in Michigan and leave Florida behind.

items.title: Florida man accused of picking saw palmetto berries without permission
items.comment: Harvesting saw palmetto berries without a state permit is a third-degree felony in Florida, punishable by up to five years. A Florida man is now finding that out over a load of berries.

items.title: MD Woman Fined For Feeding Vultures Raw Meat In Her Backyard: Report
items.comment: A Maryland woman was fined for setting out raw meat in her backyard for the vultures. Feeding the neighborhood is a virtue right up until the neighborhood is vultures.

items.title: Florida man caught speeding claimed he was rushing to Buc-ee's bathroom, deputies say
items.comment: A deputy clocked him at 117 in a 70 on I-95, and he explained he was racing to the bathroom at Buc-ee's — 60 miles away. The sheriff allowed that the bathrooms are exceptionally clean, but suggested picking one closer than an hour out.

items.title: Florida man caught speeding claimed he was rushing to Buc-ee's bathroom, deputies say
items.comment: A deputy clocked him at 117 in a 70 on I-95, and he explained he was racing to the bathroom at Buc-ee's — 60 miles away. The sheriff allowed that the bathrooms are exceptionally clean, but suggested picking one closer than an hour out.

items.title: $17K worth of cards stolen from Fanatics Fest, Florida man arrested: police
items.comment: A Florida man is accused of walking out of Fanatics Fest in Manhattan with $17,000 in trading cards. He traveled a long way to be the guy who ruins a card show.

items.title: Florida man flushed cocaine down toilet but still arrested, police say
items.comment: A Florida man flushed his cocaine down the toilet as officers arrived, which he clearly believed would settle the matter. Police arrested him anyway.

items.title: YouTube sued in major lawsuit over 'no interruptions' ad-free Premium subscription
items.comment: YouTube is being sued over the Premium tier it sold as ad-free with 'no interruptions.' The complaint is that the interruptions kept coming anyway.

items.title: Watch: Deer wanders into Pennsylvania s Hersheypark
items.comment: A deer let itself into Hersheypark and wandered the midway among the visitors. It did not, as far as anyone reported, get in line for anything.

items.title: Baltimore woman's $228K water bill dispute deepens after DPW admits HOA manages account
items.comment: A Baltimore woman is fighting a $228,000 water bill, and the dispute got worse when the city's public works department admitted its HOA billing was wrong. The meter reads like a mortgage.

items.title: Florida man suspected in tequila theft busted for DUI, sheriff says
items.comment: The man deputies were hunting as the 'tequila bandit' — thousands of dollars in liquor stuffed into a backpack — was picked up before they could get to him. He had been pulled over in the next county for driving under the influence.

items.title: Look: Escaped alligator found wandering loose in Indiana
items.comment: A four-foot alligator turned up at 2 a.m. on a downtown Jeffersonville street and settled in at the front windows of a law office. Police already knew the owner — the gator has escaped before.

items.title: Florida man dressed as Superman put in cuffs after confession: video
items.comment: Deputies found their boat-burglary suspect in a full Superman costume, cape included, and he promptly confessed to taking three power tools. The Man of Steel posted $5,500 bond.

items.title: ‘DOWN WITH THE FLOCK:’ Florida man uses simple trick to combat Flock cameras
items.comment: A 77-year-old St. Petersburg retiree taped a DOWN WITH FLOCK CAMERAS sign to a 12-foot pool skimmer, set up a lawn chair beneath the surveillance pole, and blocked the lens without touching it. Police confirmed there is nothing illegal about any of it.

items.title: Florida steakhouse touts clothing-optional Nude Dining Experience
items.comment: A Hollywood steakhouse now runs a clothing-optional dinner on the first Monday of every month, at $150 to $300 a seat. The city confirms it is legal, the staff stay dressed, and management stresses there is to be no touchy-feely stuff.

items.title: Florida man arrested after sending 7 former co-workers’ paychecks to his own bank account, deputies say
items.comment: A Florida man allegedly rerouted seven former co-workers' paychecks into his own account. It is a bold way to stay on the payroll of a job you no longer have.

items.title: Florida man arrested for illegally importing Texas livestock amid screwworm emergency, state officials say
items.comment: A Florida man is accused of running Texas livestock past inspection during a screwworm emergency — the flesh-eating parasite those checkpoints exist to catch. The paperwork he allegedly skipped was the entire point of the paperwork.

items.title: Florida man with a flamethrower barricades himself in an RV at a Walmart, cops say
items.comment: A Florida man barricaded himself inside an RV in a New Jersey Walmart parking lot, reportedly with a flamethrower for company. Crisis negotiators worked him for sixteen hours before police settled it with pepper spray.

items.title: ‘Not too good at math’: Florida man arrested for DUI after running from crash, police say
items.comment: A Daytona Beach man ran from his own crash, then warned the officers asking for his ID that they were going to get sued. The roadside sobriety test went about as well as the headline suggests.

items.title: Removing Florida man’s derelict boats has cost the state $370,000, report says
items.comment: One man's abandoned boats have cost Florida more than $370,000 to pull out of the water. Thirteen investigations and 24 unpaid citations later, the state got around to arresting him.

items.title: Driverless Stolen Porsche Takes the LAPD on a Bizarre Chase
items.comment: Unable to start the stolen Porsche, the thief simply strapped it to a pickup and towed it off. LAPD chased the truck across North Hollywood while the driverless Porsche scraped along behind, until the strap snapped and it coasted to a stop outside a car wash.

items.title: Woman goes to Waffle House. Her waffle order is so weird that 4 workers come over to ‘judge’ how she eats it: ‘Mind you they've seen it all’
items.comment: A woman cut her waffle into chips, mixed the syrup into the butter container, and dipped them like nachos. Four Waffle House employees — people who have seen everything — stopped working to come watch.

items.title: Mesa homeowners fined over backyard sunshade, now at odds with city zoning
items.comment: A Mesa couple put up a backyard sunshade to survive an Arizona summer and drew a $50 HOA fine for skipping the paperwork. Now the city's zoning code has opinions about it too.

items.title: Look: Florida police chase down loose emu wandering Dade City
items.comment: Dade City officers spent a morning running down an emu that had decided it was a fine day for a stroll through town. The department conceded that chasing an emu was not covered at the academy, then posted photos of the bird riding in a patrol car.

items.title: Towel, tequila and trouble: Jupiter man accused of bizarre early morning break-in
items.comment: A Jupiter man allegedly broke into a neighbor's house at dawn to slice a lime and pour himself her tequila, a towel wrapped around his head. He lives just down the street; a Ring camera caught him trying the front door first, six-pack in hand.

items.title: Boise Police Make Arrest Following 'Bizarre' Viral Car Crash
items.comment: After a Boise fender-bender, the driver was filmed sprinting to a storm drain to stuff something down it. A police officer later recognized the viral clip online, checked the drain, and recovered the meth he'd hidden.

items.title: Neighbor reports man's backyard vegetable garden as a farm, then HOA hears who he fed
items.comment: A neighbor talked the HOA into branding a backyard vegetable garden an illegal 'farm.' The complaint collapsed the moment the board learned the harvest had been going, free, to elderly neighbors all summer.

items.title: City Council explores temporary grazing permit ordinance for goats used to clear brush
items.comment: A city council is weighing a permit system for the goats brought in to eat the brush. Somewhere a new form now exists for livestock landscaping.

items.title: ‘I love y’all’: Florida man arrested after attempting to burglarize home with hammer, deputies say
items.comment: A hammer-wielding Florida man refused to drop it until a police drone talked deputies onto him. Cuffed at last, he offered the arrest a warm 'I love y'all.'

items.title: Florida Man Charged After Trying to Sell Sea Turtle Shell on Facebook
items.comment: A Florida man tried to move a protected hawksbill sea turtle shell on Facebook Marketplace for $2,700. The 'rare, perfect condition' listing doubled as the state's evidence.

items.title: Watch: Seattle s round raccoon Jimothy becomes viral star
items.comment: A Seattle raccoon named Jimothy went viral for a shortened spine that makes him almost perfectly round. The city didn't adopt a mascot so much as quietly surrender to one.

items.title: Influencer battles HOA lawsuit over inherited home as Jacksonville 55+ neighbors face $155K bill
items.comment: An influencer inherited a home in a Jacksonville 55-plus community, and the HOA is suing to keep her out. The bylaws, it turns out, outrank the will.

items.title: Ambulance joy ride? That’s what one Florida man is accused of doing
items.comment: A Florida man is accused of helping himself to an ambulance straight out of a Jacksonville fire station. It's one way to get somewhere fast without the copay.

items.title: Bizarre police chase ends with suspect swimming off Malibu coast
items.comment: A police chase in Malibu ended the only way California allows — the suspect bailing out and swimming off the coast. Deputies, as a rule, do not follow into the Pacific.

items.title: Ditching his 'Whizzinator' in a patrol car was Florida man's second bad decision of day | OutKick
items.comment: A Florida man repaid a deputy's courtesy — cuffs moved to the front for his sore shoulder — by yanking a fake-urine rig out of his pants and flinging it across the patrol car. It was, the sheriff noted, his second bad decision of the day.

items.title: Florida man arrested for allegedly stealing over $200,000 in crypto using Steam game malware
items.comment: A Florida man allegedly buried malware in Steam games and drained $220,000 in crypto across 8,000 devices. The FBI unraveled it by following the stolen Bitcoin to his Uber Eats orders.

items.title: Florida man arrested after being found nude behind New Smyrna Beach Circle K
items.comment: A Florida man turned up nude behind a New Smyrna Beach Circle K with no explanation on file. No word on what he came to buy, or why it required taking everything off.

items.title: Florida man repeatedly caught driving with suspended license arrested again: FCSO
items.comment: His license is suspended; his commitment to driving is not. Deputies keep finding him behind the wheel — the one place he's not allowed to be.

items.title: Central Florida man accused of impersonating nurse arrested again
items.comment: A Central Florida man was booked again for playing nurse without the license — or the training. "Again" is doing a lot of work in that sentence.

items.title: Two brothers say neighbors continue to dump on their property but they're getting fined
items.comment: Neighbors keep dumping on the brothers' land, and it's the brothers collecting the fines. The system found the victim first and stopped looking.

items.title: Homeowner Faces $100 Fine for Flying American Flag in California HOA
items.comment: Nothing says land of the free like a $100 penalty for the flag out front. The HOA reviewed the Stars and Stripes and found them non-compliant.

items.title: Florida man rode a tractor straight into a crash, and the bodycam caught it
items.comment: A Florida man took a tractor out for a spin that deputies' bodycam confirms ended in a crash. Top speed was never the risk here; direction was.

items.title: Florida man switched seats during a traffic stop, and the car rolled into the deputy's cruiser
items.comment: Pulled over, a Florida man tried the classic move of switching seats so it wouldn't look like he'd been driving. Mid-shuffle the car slipped into gear and rolled into the deputy's cruiser, settling the question of who was in control.

items.title: Florida man used a stolen debit card on Amazon to buy door hinges and Axe body spray
items.comment: Using a debit card someone left in a propane machine outside a Walmart, a Palm Coast man ordered about $79 of door hinges and Axe body spray on Amazon. He denied everything to deputies — right up until he pulled up his own Amazon account to prove his innocence and displayed the fraudulent orders for them.

items.title: Florida man arrested for trying to steal a septic tank
items.comment: A Florida man decided the one thing missing from his life was someone else's septic tank, and set out to correct the oversight. Deputies caught up with him before the plan could reach its deeply unpleasant conclusion.

items.title: An HOA fined a neighbor for having too many packages on the front porch
items.comment: Someone on the HOA board looked at a porch with a few too many delivery boxes and reached, naturally, for the fine book. Nothing rattles a homeowners association quite like visible proof that people buy things.

items.title: 'Abe Lincoln' fined for reciting the Gettysburg Address at the Lincoln Memorial
items.comment: A man dressed as Abraham Lincoln was fined for standing at the Lincoln Memorial and reciting the Gettysburg Address. The National Park Service, it turns out, requires a permit for that, and Honest Abe did not have one.

items.title: Washington Post class action alleges customer data was used to set subscription prices
items.comment: A class action claims The Washington Post quietly used customers' own data to decide how much to charge each of them for a subscription. Democracy dies in darkness; your personalized price, apparently, is set there too.

items.title: Adobe reaches $150 million settlement over termination fees and subscription cancellations
items.comment: Adobe agreed to a $150 million settlement over claims it buried the cancel button and larded subscriptions with surprise termination fees. It turns out the hardest thing Adobe ever shipped was a way to actually leave.

items.title: Parents can be fined or charged for their kids' bad behavior in a South Jersey town
items.comment: A South Jersey town passed a rule letting it fine, and even charge, parents when their children misbehave in public. The plan to cure youthful mischief is, essentially, to bill the nearest available adult for it.

items.title: Florida man arrested after trying a TikTok challenge inside a Walmart
items.comment: A Florida man was arrested after attempting a TikTok challenge inside a Walmart, trading potential likes for an actual mugshot. The algorithm giveth engagement; the deputies taketh it away.

items.title: Florida man arrested after joyriding a lawnmower through a Target store
items.comment: A Florida man was arrested after joyriding a lawn mower through the aisles of a Target, cutting precisely nothing along the way. It was, at the very least, the most groundskeeping that Target's floors will ever receive.

items.title: Iowa restaurateur's lake house HOA dispute leaves him on hook for $1M-plus in legal fees
items.comment: An Iowa restaurateur's dispute with his lake-house homeowners association has left him staring down more than a million dollars in legal fees. The house was supposed to be where he relaxed; instead it became a seven-figure hobby.

items.title: 'Lazy Landlord List': Released by the City of Albuquerque to highlight fined landlords
items.comment: The city of Albuquerque decided the sharpest tool against negligent landlords was public humiliation, so it published an official 'Lazy Landlord List.' It is government by group-chat energy, now with a municipal masthead.

items.title: Disabled veteran fights homeowners association lawsuit over flagpole in Florida yard
items.comment: A disabled veteran in Florida is fighting his homeowners association in court over the radical act of putting a flagpole in his own yard. The HOA has decided that the real threat to the neighborhood is a man and his flag.

items.title: Man found to have violated Walla Walla's chalk-use ordinance, fined $5,000
items.comment: A Walla Walla man was found to have violated the city's chalk-use ordinance and fined five thousand dollars, a remarkable price for a sidewalk. Somewhere there is a municipal code that ranks washable chalk as a $5,000 offense, and a man who found it the hard way.

items.title: Arizona homeowner fined $100 repeatedly for giving out free water in the heat amid clash with HOA
items.comment: An Arizona man kept getting hit with $100 fines for the crime of handing out free water to people in the desert heat. His homeowners association looked at a neighbor giving away cold water in summer and saw, above all else, a violation.

items.title: A burglar broke into a Brooklyn home, kissed the tenant, and ran off
items.comment: He broke in, kissed the tenant, and fled into the night without taking a single thing — a burglary in form only. Detectives are now investigating a crime whose apparent motive is, simply, affection.

items.title: NYPD is looking into people who keep emerging from manholes at night
items.comment: Somewhere beneath the city, people keep climbing out of manholes after dark, and the NYPD would very much like to know why. So far the department has plenty of sightings, a growing case file, and absolutely no explanation.

items.title: A failing robot-cop company is now publishing AI fan-fiction about its own robots
items.comment: Unable to make its security robots actually fight crime, the struggling company has pivoted to publishing AI-generated fan-fiction in which they heroically do. It is the rare business plan where the product works flawlessly, provided it stays fictional.

items.title: Florida man stole Smokey Bear signs and tried to sell them on Facebook
items.comment: Only you can prevent forest fires; only he could look at the signs warning about it and see resale inventory. He pried loose the Smokey Bear placards and listed them online, which is precisely how the authorities found them too.

items.title: Florida man arrested for driving in reverse down a busy road
items.comment: Every road is technically one-way if you are committed enough to reverse down the entire length of it, and he was extremely committed. Police disagreed with the interpretation and arrested him heading, briefly, forward.

items.title: Homeowner faced $500-a-day HOA fines over an unapproved door
items.comment: Five hundred dollars a day, indefinitely, over a single door the homeowners association had not personally signed off on. It ultimately took a brand-new state law to switch the meter off.

items.title: HOA fines an Arizona man for keeping a cooler in his own driveway
items.comment: A man kept a cooler in his own driveway, and his HOA responded with fines, because nothing threatens property values quite like accessible cold beverages. The cooler stays put; the citations keep arriving.

items.title: A five-year HOA fight over a short-term rental could reach the state Supreme Court
items.comment: A single short-term rental has fueled a five-year legal war that may now climb all the way to the state Supreme Court. Somewhere, a system designed to keep neighborhoods calm is working exactly as intended.

items.title: A car ended up on a roof, and police had to explain how
items.comment: A car somehow ended up on top of a roof, forcing police to hold a straight-faced briefing to explain a sentence that should not exist. Physics did something dramatic; the roof, notably, was never consulted.

items.title: TSA issues a warning after a bizarre peanut butter incident at the airport
items.comment: The TSA issued a formal warning after a peanut butter incident strange enough to reach the national news. It spreads, it apparently sets off alarms, and it has now earned its very own airport advisory.

items.title: A lawyer took on his own HOA and ended up jailed for contempt
items.comment: He was an actual practicing attorney who took his own homeowners association to court, and somehow walked out jailed for contempt instead. He knew the law; the HOA knew the judge, and the HOA remains undefeated.

items.title: Florida man arrested for trespassing while wearing an actual jail outfit
items.comment: He was arrested for trespassing while already dressed, head to toe, in a genuine jail outfit, which is either terrible luck or excellent planning. Dress for the job you want; he was, at minimum, fully prepared for booking.

items.title: Florida man arrested for burglary on his way to court for a different burglary
items.comment: He was arrested for a fresh burglary while on his way to court to answer for a previous one, which is at least thematically consistent. Time management is hard, but he did technically make both appointments.

items.title: Florida man tries to lawyer his way out of a traffic stop — by pretending to be a lawyer
items.comment: He had no bar card, no firm, and no case — just the unshakable confidence of a man who decided to represent himself on the shoulder of the highway. The deputies, it turns out, were not persuaded by opposing counsel.

items.title: Family fined by their HOA for a Christmas lights display
items.comment: Nothing says peace on earth quite like a homeowners association citation for displaying too much holiday cheer. The lights stayed up, the neighbors stayed festive, and the invoice stayed firmly in the mailbox.
items.source_name: ABC News - Breaking News, Latest News and Videos

items.title: Florida man fights the deputies pulling him out of an 'alligator-infested' canal
items.comment: Deputies pulled him out of a canal they described as alligator-infested, and he thanked them by fighting the people doing the rescuing. He wanted to stay; the alligators, the deputies, and basic survival instinct all disagreed.

items.title: Restaurant fined for hiding its health alert behind a potted plant
items.comment: The health-code violation was bad enough, but the real artistry was concealing the official alert behind a single, strategically placed potted plant. Inspectors found both the violation and the houseplant defense thoroughly unconvincing.

items.title: A $100 HOA fine took years of court battles to resolve
items.comment: A hundred-dollar fine escalated into years of court battles and untold billable hours, all to resolve a sum you could find in a couch cushion. Everyone technically won, and the $100 remains completely undefeated.

items.title: A whale sinks a fire boat in Raritan Bay
items.comment: A whale collided with a fire boat in Raritan Bay and sent the vessel straight to the bottom, an outcome that is genuinely difficult to phrase in an incident report. The boat lost decisively, and the whale was never so much as questioned.

items.title: Town moves to fine parents when their kids break e-bike laws
items.comment: When kids break the local e-bike laws, the town's bold new plan is to hand the ticket to their parents instead. It's accountability, thoughtfully outsourced one full generation upward.

items.title: HOA fines residents for flying the American flag
items.comment: Residents were fined by their homeowners association for the deeply subversive act of flying the American flag on American soil. The most American thing in the whole story isn't the flag — it's the fine for the flag.

items.title: Florida man pulled over with 34 open White Claws on the passenger seat
items.comment: He was pulled over with thirty-four open White Claws riding shotgun, a figure that is neither casual nor easily explained to a deputy. Not one, not a sensible six — the passenger seat was clearly having a bigger night than he was.

items.title: Restaurant fined under a 'no dancing' law, launches a petition
items.comment: A restaurant got fined under an actual, still-enforced 'no dancing' ordinance and answered the only sensible way: by launching a petition. It's Footloose in real life, except the town wins the opening act and the fine is entirely, boringly real.

items.title: 'Cop Santa Claus' hauls in a pair of suspected Christmas tree thieves
items.comment: An officer in a full Santa Claus getup personally hauled in a pair of suspected Christmas tree thieves, which is almost too on-the-nose to be real. Santa now knows who's been naughty and, apparently, holds arrest powers; the trees were recovered.

items.title: Homeowner sues his HOA over $80,000 in fines, 'and counting'
items.comment: His homeowners association fines started small and quietly metastasized past eighty thousand dollars, so he is finally suing to make it stop. 'And counting' is doing a truly heroic amount of work in that sentence.

items.title: Florida man leads a chase, then drives his SUV straight into a pond
items.comment: He led police on a chase that was going reasonably well right up until he steered his SUV directly into a pond. The plan was flawless until the water; the SUV has filed no comment since.

items.title: Burglary suspect undone by a hilariously dumb escape error
items.comment: The burglary itself was nearly flawless, right up until an escape blunder dumb enough to carry the entire police write-up. The crime was almost perfect; the exit strategy very much was not.
